name: BQ25798RQMR
title: 1-to-4-cell 5 A buck-boost charger, I2C controlled, with two-input mux, solar MPPT and backup mode
summary: The BQ25798 is an I2C-programmed buck-boost charger for 1 to 4 Li-ion or Li-polymer cells, with the four converter switches, the battery FET, both current-sense paths and loop compensation on the die. It runs from 3.6 V to 24 V (30 V tolerant), charges at up to 5 A in 10 mA steps and keeps the system rail up with NVDC power-path control. Two gate drivers select between two inputs through external back-to-back N-FETs, an open-circuit-voltage MPPT routine suits small solar panels, and the same converter runs in reverse for 2.8 V to 22 V OTG output or an automatic backup supply. A 16-bit ADC reports currents, voltages and temperatures.

pins.name: STAT
pins.function: Charge status. Low while charging; high when charging is done or disabled; toggles at 1 Hz on a fault. Pull up through 10 kΩ. DIS_STAT = 1 turns the function off.

pins.name: VBUS
pins.function: Charger input. The input current sense sits between VBUS and PMID. Recommended decoupling: two 10 µF and one 0.1 µF ceramic, the 0.1 µF right at the IC.

pins.name: BTST1
pins.function: Bootstrap supply for the input-side high-side switch Q1: a 47 nF ceramic of 10 V or more from SW1 to BTST1.

pins.name: REGN
pins.function: Internal LDO output, fed from whichever of VBUS and BAT is higher. Supplies the gate drivers and the TS divider bias. Bypass with a 10 V, 4.7 µF ceramic to power ground.

pins.name: D+
pins.function: USB D+ line for detection on the VIN1 input: data contact detection, BC1.2 primary and secondary detection and the high-voltage adapter handshake.

pins.name: D-
pins.function: USB D- line for detection on the VIN1 input, with the same functions as D+.

pins.name: VAC2
pins.function: Port 2 input sense. A voltage from 3.6 V to 24 V marks a valid source on port 2. Tie to VBUS when ACFET2 and RBFET2 are not fitted.

pins.name: VAC1
pins.function: Port 1 input sense. A voltage from 3.6 V to 24 V marks a valid source on port 1. Tie to VBUS when ACFET1 and RBFET1 are not fitted.

pins.name: ACDRV2
pins.function: Charge-pump gate drive for the port 2 back-to-back N-FETs (ACFET2 and RBFET2); raises their gates 5 V above the common source to turn them on. Tie to GND when the pair is absent.

pins.name: ACDRV1
pins.function: Charge-pump gate drive for the port 1 back-to-back N-FETs (ACFET1 and RBFET1); raises their gates 5 V above the common source to turn them on. Tie to GND when the pair is absent.

pins.name: QON
pins.function: Ship FET wake and system reset input, active low, pulled up internally through RQON (3.6 V to 3.8 V typ with VBUS and VBAT above 5 V). Low for tSM_EXIT leaves ship mode; low for tRST turns the ship FET off for tRST_SFET (charger in HIZ if VBUS is present), sinks 30 mA from SYS, then turns it back on.

pins.name: CE
pins.function: Charge enable, active low. Charging needs CE low and EN_CHG = 1. Drive it high or low; it must not float.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: I2C clock. Pull up to the logic rail through 10 kΩ.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: I2C data. Pull up to the logic rail through 10 kΩ.

pins.name: TS
pins.function: Battery thermistor input. An NTC (a 103AT 10 kΩ part is the recommended one) with a divider from REGN to TS to GND sets the temperature window; charging pauses outside it.

pins.name: ILIM_HIZ
pins.function: Input current limit and HIZ control. A divider from a pull-up rail sets VILIM_HIZ = 1 V + 800 mΩ × IINDPM; the lower of this and the IINDPM register applies. Below 0.75 V the converter stops switching with REGN still on; above 1 V it switches again. Tie to REGN for the highest limit.

pins.name: BATP
pins.function: Battery voltage sense, to the pack positive terminal through a 100 Ω series resistor.

pins.name: BTST2
pins.function: Bootstrap supply for the output-side high-side switch Q4: a 47 nF ceramic of 10 V or more from SW2 to BTST2.

pins.name: PROG
pins.function: Power-on default program. A resistor to ground (1 % or 2 %) read at power-up picks the default switching frequency and cell count (see the PROG table).

pins.name: INT
pins.function: Interrupt to the host: an active-low 256 µs pulse on status changes and faults. Pull up through 10 kΩ.

pins.name: BAT
pins.function: Battery power connection to the pack positive terminal. The charge current sense sits between SYS and BAT. Recommended decoupling: two 10 µF ceramic.

pins.name: SDRV
pins.function: Gate drive for an external N-channel ship FET: on whenever ship mode is off, off in ship and shutdown modes. Without a ship FET, fit a 1 nF, 50 V, 0402 ceramic from SDRV to GND.

pins.name: SYS
pins.function: System output. Drain of the internal high-side switch Q4 (source on SW2). Recommended decoupling: five 10 µF and one 0.1 µF ceramic, the 0.1 µF right at the IC.

pins.name: SW2
pins.function: Boost-side switching node, between Q3 and Q4; to the inductor.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground.

pins.name: SW1
pins.function: Buck-side switching node, between Q1 and Q2; to the inductor.

pins.name: PMID
pins.function: Drain of the internal high-side switch Q1 (source on SW1). Recommended decoupling: three 10 µF and one 0.1 µF ceramic, the 0.1 µF right at the IC; for backup mode add two 33 µF POSCAPs to hold PMID through the changeover.

operation.text: Bias comes from the higher of VBUS and VBAT. The part wakes once VBUS passes VVBUS_UVLOZ or VBAT passes VBAT_UVLOZ; if neither is high enough but VAC1 or VAC2 is above VAC_PRESENT, it runs from whichever VAC came up first.

At power-on the resistor on PROG fixes the default switching frequency and cell count, and through the cell count the defaults of ICHG (1 A), VSYSMIN and VREG. VREG may only be written within the window for the present CELL setting (1s 3 V to 4.99 V, 2s 5 V to 9.99 V, 3s 10 V to 13.99 V, 4s 14 V to 18.8 V); writes outside are ignored. Changing CELL reloads ICHG, VSYSMIN and VREG with that cell count's defaults, and REG_RST or a watchdog expiry later returns them to the CELL defaults, not the PROG ones.

With only a battery above VBAT_UVLOZ, the BATFET connects it to SYS while REGN stays off to save current. About 5 ms after VBAT passes the threshold the part looks for ACFET-RBFET pairs, reads PROG and loads its registers; I2C opens at about 20 ms; then the BATFET turns on.

Power-on starts at VBUS > VVBUS_UVLOZ (direct input) or VACx > VAC_PRESENT. At about 5 ms it checks for FET pairs, reads PROG and loads defaults, then turns on any pair found. I2C opens at about 20 ms. VBUS_PRESENT_STAT sets when VBUS passes VVBUS_UVLOZ and REGN comes on about 150 ms later. Poor-source qualification follows (about 30 ms), PG_STAT sets, the ADC reads ILIM_HIZ and VBUS to load IINDPM and VINDPM, D+/D- detection runs, and the converter starts about 30 ms after detection ends.

From VBUS, REGN runs when VVBUS_PRESENT < VBUS < VVBUS_OVP. On battery alone it runs only in OTG mode, or with VBAT above 3.2 V and the TS ADC channel on. REGN feeds the gate drivers; the ILIM_HIZ, TS and STAT pull-ups may use it, but nothing else should. INT is better pulled to an external 1.8 V or 3.3 V rail because REGN can be off on battery power.

Once REGN is up the input must stay below VVBUS_OVP and above VPOORSRC while IPOORSRC is drawn. A pass sets PG_STAT and pulses INT. An overvoltage sets VBUS_OVP_STAT and its flag and retries when it clears. A poor source sets EN_HIZ and PG_FLAG, pulses INT unless PG_MASK is set, and is retried every 7 minutes; clearing EN_HIZ or replugging forces an immediate retry.

Before switching starts the ADC reads ILIM_HIZ and turns it into a current limit that caps IINDPM; the host cannot write IINDPM above that cap unless EN_EXTILIM = 0. The pin may be biased from REGN or any other rail. Pulling it below 0.75 V stops the converter in both forward and OTG modes with REGN on; above 1 V it resumes.

Right after D+/D- detection the ADC measures unloaded VBUS (VBUS0) and sets VINDPM 1.4 V below it (VBUS0 ≥ 7 V) or 0.7 V below it (VBUS0 < 7 V), clamped to 3.6 V to 22 V. FORCE_VINDPM_DET repeats the measurement, but only when VSYS_STAT = 0 (battery above VSYSMIN); otherwise the bit clears and VINDPM is kept.

Detection runs on the VAC1 input only and only with AUTO_INDET_EN = 1. It follows BC1.2 for SDP, CDP and DCP and recognises four non-standard divider adapters, then sets IINDPM and VBUS_STAT. It takes 500 ms for a legacy port up to 2 s for HVDCP. A CDP needs enumeration within 2.5 s or it falls back to SDP; the host must handle that. The host may rewrite IINDPM afterwards; the lower of IINDPM and ILIM_HIZ always applies. FORCE_INDET reruns detection.

After a DCP is found the part can ask the adapter for 9 V (EN_9V) or 12 V (EN_12V); with both set it tries 12 V first. Because DCP detection loads 3.25 A first, which can upset the step up, the recommended flow is: keep HVDCP_EN = 0 at plug-in; on a DCP result (VBUS_STAT = 0011) set IINDPM to 1.5 A and then HVDCP_EN = 1; afterwards return HVDCP_EN to 0.

DPLUS_DAC and DMINUS_DAC drive D+ and D- to fixed levels (HIZ, 0 V, 0.6 V, 1.2 V, 2.0 V, 2.7 V, 3.3 V, or D+ shorted to D-), and the ADC reads both lines back. Writes are ignored while detection is running.

ACDRV1 and ACDRV2 drive optional back-to-back N-FET pairs on two inputs. A pair turns on only if it was found at power-on, its VAC is between VVAC_PRESENT and the VAC OVP threshold, DIS_ACDRV and EN_HIZ are 0 and VBUS is below VVBUS_PRESENT. With two pairs the first valid input wins, port 1 on a tie. The host swaps sources by exchanging EN_ACDRV1 and EN_ACDRV2 in one write (both at 1 is refused); the part opens the active pair, waits for VBUS to fall below VBUS_PRESENT and closes the other, with a short gap in switching. If the active input fails by undervoltage, overvoltage or IBUS overcurrent it swaps automatically. With one valid input, only DIS_ACDRV = 1 turns both pairs off.

The converter moves between buck, boost and buck-boost without host action according to input and system voltage. With a battery fitted SYS is held at least at VSYSMIN and follows the battery above it. With no battery and charging disabled (CE, EN_CHG or a missing thermistor), BAT idles near 2.5 V and SYS sits at VSYSMIN. With no battery, TS ignored and under 200 µF on BAT, BAT and SYS ramp up to their OVP limits and back in a sawtooth; disabling the 30 mA BAT discharge reduces its swing.

With EN_ICO = 1 the ICO searches for the largest input current that does not pull the source into VINDPM; it runs after a DCP is detected, or on FORCE_ICO. With VBAT above VSYSMIN it starts at 500 mA and climbs; below VSYSMIN it starts from the IINDPM register value and falls. The result appears in ICO_ILIM with ICO_STAT and ICO_FLAG. It reruns on a new source or EN_HIZ toggle, an IINDPM or VINDPM write, FORCE_ICO, or VBUS OVP.

With EN_MPPT = 1 the converter periodically stops for VOC_DLY, measures the open-circuit VBUS and sets VINDPM = VOC_PCT × VOC, then runs for VOC_RATE before measuring again; the battery carries the system during each pause. Setting the charge current to its maximum keeps VINDPM in control. MPPT cannot be enabled with VBAT below VSYSMIN, and it clears when VBUS falls below VBUS_PRESENT. ICO, forced VINDPM detection and MPPT exclude one another: while one is enabled the other two cannot be turned on.

At light load the converter drops into PFM. PFM_FWD_DIS = 1 keeps fixed-frequency PWM, which then goes discontinuous. With OOA on (DIS_FWD_OOA = 0) the PFM rate stays above 25 kHz. OTG mode has its own PFM_OTG_DIS and DIS_OTG_OOA. Peak inductor current in PFM is limited to 2 A with OOA on and 3.3 A with OOA off or near the PFM exit point.

EN_HIZ = 1 turns REGN off and stops switching even with an adapter present; the BATFET carries the system and the ADC is off unless re-enabled. Overvoltage on VBUS, SYS, the battery or the OTG output stops switching but keeps REGN up; VSYS_SHORT and IBUS_OCP set EN_HIZ.

OTG drives VBUS from the battery at VOTG with the IOTG current limit. It needs VBAT above VBAT_OTG and no battery OVP, VBUS below VVBUS_UVLO and TS inside the BHOT/BCOLD window. Battery discharge in OTG is regulated to IBAT_REG (3 A, 4 A, 5 A or off): above it the OTG output is cut back to favour the system load and IBAT_REG_STAT sets. The 3/4/5 A settings soft-start the OTG current; the off setting does not. Swapping OTG between ports means opening the active pair first, letting VBUS fall, then closing the other.

With VBUS present and EN_BACKUP = 1, a comparator watches VBUS; when it falls below VBUS_BACKUP × VINDPM the part forces EN_OTG = 1 and regulates VBUS/PMID at VOTG from the battery or capacitors, opens ACFET1-RBFET1 (DIS_ACDRV = 1) so the adapter is not back-driven, and reports VBUS_STAT = 1100. ACFET1-RBFET1 must be fitted or EN_BACKUP stays 0. A VAC overvoltage also moves it into backup. It exits when the stored voltage falls below VBAT_OTGZ or the host clears EN_OTG. IBAT_REG = 11 (off) gives the best response, and up to 200 µF of extra low-ESR PMID capacitance may be needed.

operation.topic: Returning from backup to the adapter
operation.text: To go back to VAC1 and re-arm: write BKUP_ACFET1_ON = 1 (sets DIS_ACDRV = 0, EN_ACDRV1 = 1; backup off, OTG still running) with the adapter at or above VOTG; confirm EN_ACDRV1 reads 1; clear EN_OTG, which also clears BKUP_ACFET1_ON and sets EN_BACKUP. This path skips poor-source, ILIM and VINDPM measurement, so VINDPM keeps its old value; allow about 5 s before re-arming. To return without re-arming, clear BKUP_ACFET1_ON before clearing EN_OTG. Returning to ACIN2 drops PMID briefly; the sequence is EN_BACKUP = 0, DIS_ACDRV = 0, EN_ACDRV2 = 1, confirm, EN_OTG = 0, then optionally EN_BACKUP = 1.

The BATFET separates SYS from the battery. Below VSYSMIN it runs as a linear regulator and SYS sits about 200 mV above VSYSMIN; above it the BATFET is fully on and SYS = VBAT + IBAT × RDS(on). With charging off or terminated SYS is held 200 mV (PWM) or 600 mV (PFM) above VBAT. VSYS_STAT is high in minimum-system regulation.

When the input cannot carry system plus charge current, IINDPM or VINDPM limits the input and the VSYSMIN loop trims charge current. If that reaches zero and SYS falls below VBAT, the BATFET turns on in ideal-diode mode (about 25 mV VDS at light current, fully on at higher current) so the battery supplements the input. It turns off below the battery depletion threshold. VINDPM_STAT and IINDPM_STAT report DPM.

With EN_CHG = 1 and CE low the part charges on its own: trickle, pre-charge, constant current, constant voltage and an optional top-off. A cycle starts when VBUS > VVBUS_PRESENT, VBAT is below the recharge level for TRECHG, charging is enabled, and there is no TS or timer fault. CHG_STAT reports the phase and every phase change pulses INT. Toggling CE or EN_CHG after termination starts a new cycle.

Below VBAT_SHORTZ (2.5 V max at BATP) the part trickle-charges at up to 100 mA, holding 2.5 V per cell for about 1.5 s to close a pack protector; above it pre-charge at IPRECHG runs until VBAT_LOWV, then fast charge. In VSYSMIN regulation with the BATFET in LDO mode, charge current is held to 2 A whatever ICHG says. DIS_LDO = 1 removes LDO mode and VSYSMIN regulation; trickle current is unaffected. VREG should not be set below VSYSMIN.

Charging ends when VBAT is above the recharge level, the voltage loop is in control and current is below ITERM; the BATFET then opens and CHG_STAT = 111. Termination is held off during IINDPM, VINDPM or TREG regulation. EN_TERM = 0 disables it and drops the battery OVP threshold from 103 % of VREG to VREG. At 40 mA to 160 mA the real termination current can be 20 % to 40 % above target; the top-off timer (off by default) keeps charging in CV for a set time after termination and follows the safety timer's suspend and half-rate rules. It resets on charge re-enable, a new termination or REG_RST.

Trickle (fixed 1 h), pre-charge (2 h or 0.5 h) and fast charge (5, 8, 12 or 24 h, default 12 h) timers start with their phase; each has an enable bit. During DPM or thermal regulation they count at half rate unless TMR2X_EN = 0, and they pause during faults that stop charging. They reset on a charge restart, a move between phases, or a change of their own setting. Expiry sets the matching STAT bit and pulses INT.

Charging needs TS between VT1 and VT5. In the cool range T1 to T2 the charge current drops to 20 %, 40 % or 100 % of ICHG or stops (JEITA_ISETC); in the warm range T3 to T5 the current follows JEITA_ISETH and the voltage is reduced by 0 mV to 800 mV or charging stops (JEITA_VSET). VT2 and VT3 are programmable (TS_COOL, TS_WARM); VT1 and VT5 are fixed. Termination still works in those ranges, and the safety timer runs at half rate when current is cut to 20 % or 40 %. TS_IGNORE = 1 treats TS as always good.

In OTG mode the battery must stay between VBCOLD and VBHOT (defaults -10 °C and 60 °C with the 5.24 kΩ / 30.31 kΩ network). Outside it the converter stops with EN_OTG still 1, VBUS_STAT reads 000 and TS_COLD_STAT or TS_HOT_STAT sets; REGN stays on and OTG resumes when the temperature returns.

ADC_EN starts the 16-bit ADC; ADC_RATE picks continuous or one-shot, and a one-shot run clears ADC_EN when done. It works with VBUS > 3.4 V or VBAT > 2.9 V (3.2 V on battery alone with the TS channel on), including in HIZ. Channels: IBUS, IBAT, VBUS, VAC1, VAC2, VBAT, VSYS, TS, TDIE, D+ and D-; each can be turned off, and a disabled channel keeps its last reading. For lowest current turn the ADC off with ADC_EN rather than disabling all channels. Changing ADC_SAMPLE mid-run restarts the channel in progress. ADC_DONE_STAT and its flag are meaningful in one-shot mode only. Readings are for DC conditions.

STAT is low while charging, high when done, disabled, in HIZ, battery-only or OTG, and blinks at 1 Hz on a fault that stops charging. INT gives a 256 µs low pulse on a good source appearing or leaving, VBUS_STAT changes, IINDPM, VINDPM or TREG entry, watchdog expiry (also at first power-up), charge status and TS changes, the OVP, OCP and thermal-shutdown faults, safety-timer expiry and a rising edge on any other STAT bit. Each source has a STAT bit (present state), a FLAG bit (latched, cleared when read) and a MASK bit (stops the pulse).

SDRV is a charge pump (about 100 nA) that drives an external ship FET gate about 5 V above the battery, at roughly 50 % duty on battery alone. SDRV_CTRL picks: 00 idle (FET on); 01 shutdown (FET off, I2C off, wakes only on adapter insertion, refused with an adapter present); 10 ship mode (FET off, I2C on with a slow clock; exits on adapter insertion, SDRV_CTRL = 00, REG_RST or QON low for tSM_EXIT); 11 system power reset (FET off for about 350 ms, charger in HIZ if VBUS is present, 30 mA sink on SYS, then back on and SDRV_CTRL returns to 00). The off action can be delayed 10 s by SDRV_DLY. QON low for tRST (about 10 s) also resets system power.

VAC OVP opens that input's FET pair and moves to the other valid input if there is one. VBUS OVP (26 V typ) stops switching and the BATFET carries the system until it clears. A poor source stops switching and is retried every 7 minutes. SYS OVP stops switching until SYS returns. Below VSYS_SHORT (2.2 V typ) the converter output current is held under 1 A. Battery OVP (104 % of VREG) stops the converter until VBAT falls to 102 %. Battery discharge OCP needs a ship FET, SFET_PRESENT = 1 and EN_BATOC = 1, and then opens the ship FET. IBUS OCP (8 A typ, EN_IBUS_OCP = 1) sets EN_HIZ and DIS_ACDRV, which the host or a replug must clear. OTG OVP stops switching until VBUS falls back; OTG UVP shuts down for 500 ms and retries. Each fault sets its STAT and FLAG bits and pulses INT unless masked.

Above the TREG setting (60 °C to 120 °C) charge or OTG current is reduced to hold the junction there; termination is suspended, the fast-charge timer runs at half rate and TREG_STAT sets. Above TSHUT the converter turns off, and it restarts once the die has cooled by TSHUT_HYS.

Target address 0x6B (1101011b), registers 00h to 48h; reads above 48h return FFh and an undefined address is NACKed. Standard (100 kbit/s) and fast (400 kbit/s) modes are supported, with fixed logic thresholds and a 1.5 s timeout on an unfinished transaction. Multi-byte reads and writes may cross register boundaries, so a 49-byte read from 00h dumps the whole map.

operation.topic: Host mode, default mode and watchdog
operation.text: After power-on the part is in default mode (watchdog expired, WD_STAT high) and charges with default settings and timers. Any I2C write moves it to host mode and starts the watchdog; the host keeps it there by writing WD_RST before expiry or by setting WATCHDOG = 000. On expiry the part returns to default mode, resets the watchdog-reset registers, sets WD_STAT and WD_FLAG and pulses INT. REG_RST resets the REG_RST-marked registers, stops a forced ICO, VINDPM or D+/D- detection, and does not repeat FET-pair detection or the VINDPM measurement.

1.5 MHz operation is for a 1 µH inductor and 750 kHz for 2.2 µH, and each frequency works only with its inductor. Saturation current must cover the larger of input or charge (OTG: discharge or output) current plus half the ripple, and at least 2 A. Input (PMID) and SYS capacitors should be low-ESR X5R/X7R ceramics: 1 × 0.1 µF + 3 × 10 µF at PMID rated 25 V or more for up to 20 V and 3.3 A input, plus 2 × 33 µF POSCAP for backup mode; 1 × 0.1 µF + 5 × 10 µF at SYS, 16 V or more for 2s, for up to 5 A charging. Input ripple is worst at D = 0.5; output ripple at the lowest VBUS.

The panel open-circuit voltage must stay under the 24 V operating limit, so 6 V, 9 V and 12 V panels fit. VOC_PCT is set from the panel's VMPP/VOC ratio: for VOC = 10 V and VMPP = 8 V (80 %), VOC_PCT = 4 (81.25 %) is the starting point.
SYS needs either a 3.6 V to 24 V input rated above 500 mA on VBUS or a 1s to 4s Li-ion battery above VBAT_UVLO on BAT. Full output power to SYS needs a source of at least 3 A.

In order: put 0402 or 0201 0.1 µF capacitors on the IC's own layer right at PMID-GND and SYS-GND, ideally with a 10 µF beside each and the rest tied in with low impedance; route SW1 and SW2 through vias under the IC to the inductor on another layer with as little copper as will carry the current, and the BTST capacitors may use those vias; place the REGN capacitor close with at least two ground vias; put a 0.1 µF at VBUS with two ground vias and the 10 µF parts further out; place the battery capacitors tight to the BAT and ground pins; size vias for the current; keep BATP and TS away from SW1 and SW2.
